main_text.p: dissimæ[?] densissimis quasi nubibus obteguntur: aures obsurdescunt: manus, quæ corpus custodiunt, tremere incipiunt: crura, quibus idem nititur, sub pondere vacillant.

VIII. In ea autem quæ à fortuna manant, atque proficiscuntur, an non vim suam atq; tyrannidem tempus exercet: dum facultatibus homines exuit: dum quos terra profert fructus conterit & corrumpit: dum præclarorum virorum memoriam oblivione extinguit?
IX. Iam vero rei literariæ quantam idem tempus cladem intulerit, quis ignorat?
X. Quære Aristotelis plus quàm quingentos libros, qui à doctis numerantur: nusquam apparebùt: quæ rerum gestarum scriptores, quorum suis in scriptis mentionem Cicero facit: non reperies.
XI. In tempore porrò corruptis depravatisq; locis emendandis quàm viri doctissimi clarissimiq; sunt hodie, & quàm hæc in re de literis merentur præclarè?
XII. Ad Imperia verò & Respubl. conferre me si vellem, Deum immortalem quàm mihi metuendū esset, ne in orationem integram epistola excresceret.

XIII. Ubi doctæ illæ & literis literatisq; hominibus affluentes Athenæ? ubi nobilis & rebus belli- cis celeberrima Lacedæmoniorum Respublica? ubi æmula laudis Romanæ Carthago? nonne his omnibus tempus solum ruinam atq; interitum attulit?

page.notes: The first word of the page, "dissimæ", is a fragment whose start is cut off at the top of the scan; the reading is doubtful. The word is printed with a long-s ligature that reads as "ß". The page number "211" is printed as "21ı" and is only partly legible. The signature at the foot reads "O 3" but the last digit is doubtful. The ampersand in "conterit & corrumpit" and "& quàm" is the printed "et" sign. The text contains no notes in the margin.
